test_case_metadata.title: Verify user registration with valid details
test_case_metadata.description: This test case verifies that a new user can successfully register on the application by providing valid details including username, email, password, and personal information. automation_notes.complexity_justification: This is a standard user registration flow with multiple form fields and page transitions. The test involves basic form interactions (text input, button clicks), page navigation, and success message verification. Complexity is medium due to: (1) Multiple form fields requiring data entry and validation, (2) Need for unique test data generation to avoid conflicts, (3) Form submission with backend processing, (4) Page transitions requiring proper wait strategies, (5) Potential validation errors and duplicate user scenarios. No complex elements like iframes, multi-window handling, file uploads, or dynamic content are involved.

risks.risk: Test data conflicts - username or email may already exist in the system causing registration to fail
risks.mitigation: Implement dynamic test data generation using timestamps or unique identifiers. Use API to check and delete existing test users before test execution.

risks.risk: Form field locators may be dynamic or change frequently if the UI is under active development
risks.mitigation: Use data-testid attributes if available, or stable CSS selectors. Implement locator fallback strategies with multiple locator options.

risks.risk: Page load timing may vary across environments causing flaky waits and timeouts
risks.mitigation: Use explicit waits with proper conditions instead of fixed delays. Implement retry logic for transient failures.

risks.risk: Password complexity requirements may not be documented and test password may not meet requirements
risks.mitigation: Verify password requirements with development team. Use a password that meets common complexity requirements (uppercase, lowercase, number, special character, minimum length).

risks.risk: Backend registration API may have rate limiting or validation that causes intermittent failures
risks.mitigation: Add appropriate waits after form submission. Implement retry logic for transient backend errors. Monitor API response codes.

risks.risk: Success message may appear as a toast notification that auto-dismisses, making it difficult to verify
risks.mitigation: Implement fast verification immediately after form submission. Use explicit wait for success message to appear before verifying.

recommendations: Implement Page Object Model pattern with separate classes for HomePage, RegistrationPage, and ConfirmationPage containing their respective locators and action methods
Use a test data management layer that generates unique usernames and emails using timestamps or UUIDs to avoid conflicts
Implement proper wait strategies using explicit waits for all element interactions - wait for visible, enabled, and clickable states before interacting
Add screenshot capture on assertion failures for debugging and include step number and timestamp in screenshot filename
Make base URL and API URL configurable through environment configuration to support multi-environment testing
Implement API-based test data cleanup in teardown to delete test users created during test execution
Consider adding retry logic for flaky network-dependent steps like form submission
Implement comprehensive logging at each step to aid in debugging failures
Add validation for password complexity requirements before attempting registration
Consider parameterizing this test to run with multiple data sets (data-driven testing) to cover various registration scenarios
Implement a precondition check to verify application accessibility before starting the test
Use composite action methods like 'fill_registration_form' and 'complete_registration' to reduce code duplication and improve maintainability
special_handling_notes: Username and email must be unique for each test run - implement dynamic generation or cleanup strategy
Password fields are masked so value verification may need to check element attribute or length instead of visible text
Form submission may trigger backend validation - ensure proper wait for response before verifying success
Success message may be displayed as a toast notification, modal, or on a separate confirmation page - locator strategy should account for this
If the application uses CAPTCHA on registration page, this cannot be automated through standard UI interaction and will need a bypass mechanism for test environment
If email verification is required after registration, additional steps will be needed to verify email or use a test email service
